title: Delegated burst credits, soft-fence isolation, and capacity resilience PRD
creator: Asha Ramaswami
overview: This PRD defines behavior, APIs, acceptance criteria, and rollout plan for three related Dedicated capacity features: (1) delegated burst credits that allow tenants to consume a bounded extra capacity pool, (2) soft-fence tenant isolation to reduce noisy-neighbor impact without hard preemption, and (3) capacity resilience controls (adaptive eviction windows and graceful preemption) to meet SLOs while maximizing utilization.
background: Customers using Dedicated capacity have asked for more predictable isolation and controlled burst behavior. Current implementations either allow unbounded burst (risking SLO violations for reserved tenants) or hard preemption (causing failed requests). We need an approach that gives reserved tenants isolation guarantees while letting lower-priority tenants safely absorb transient capacity without catastrophic failures.
goals: 1) Define a burst credit model that is simple to reason about and billable. 2) Implement soft-fence isolation to throttle and delay non-reserved requests before preempting. 3) Provide eviction and preemption rules that preserve high-priority SLOs (p99 latency and reservation throughput) and reduce hard failures. 4) Expose configuration and observability for tenants and operators.
non_goals: 1) Full rework of reservation SLA tiers (this is an incremental capability). 2) Replacing Dedicated autoscaler; autoscaler tuning will use these primitives but is out of scope. 3) Introducing new billing models beyond simple consumed burst units in this phase.
user_stories: As a platform admin, I want a per-tenant burst credit budget with configurable refill semantics so I can cap burst costs and prevent unbounded consumption.
As a reserved-tenant owner, I want guarantees that my reserved throughput and p95/p99 latency targets will be protected during neighbour bursts.
As a low-priority tenant, I want my requests to be delayed and queued (soft-fence) rather than abruptly failed when capacity is tight.
As an on-call operator, I want clear metrics and alerting around burst consumption and preemption events so I can triage incidents quickly.
requirements: Burst credit primitives: per-tenant credit balance, max-burst-per-window, refill rate (credits/min), and a billing meter for consumed burst credits.
Soft-fence policy: configurable thresholds to move requests into delayed queue (with exponential backoff) before preemption; policy should be per-priority-class.

Preemption rules: deterministic eviction order (lowest priority, oldest burst consumer, largest recent usage) with a configurable grace period; preemption should only occur after soft-fence attempts fail for X seconds.
SLO guardrails: system must maintain reserved-tenant p99 latency within defined window for 99.9% of events over 1h rolling windows under expected load shapes specified in acceptance criteria.
Operator controls: ability to drain burst credits (emergency), increase/decrease refill rates, and opt a tenant out of burst behavior.
Observability: new dashboard panels for burst credit balance, refill rate, soft-fence queue length, preemption events, per-tenant reserved throughput, and cost attribution for burst usage.
API/UI: console controls to view and edit burst settings per-reservation and a REST API endpoint for programmatic changes and read-only telemetry.
Backward compatibility: default behavior for existing reservations must be unchanged unless tenant-level configs are set.
api_changes: Add REST endpoints: GET /v1/reservations/{id}/burst, POST /v1/reservations/{id}/burst (update), POST /v1/reservations/{id}/burst/refill (admin), GET /v1/tenants/{id}/softfence-status. API returns credit balance, refill_rate, max_burst_window, and recent_consumption. Console adds a 'Burst & Isolation' tab under reservation settings.
ux_considerations: Console will show an inline simulation: if tenant uses N burst credits/day at current refill rate, estimate monthly cost. Soft-fence state should expose current queue length and average hold-time. Default settings will be conservative (small refill) to avoid surprise billing. Inline help and guardrails required when increasing limits.
acceptance_criteria: Functional: A tenant with a 1000-req/min reservation under a synthetic burst test (incoming load 2x reservation for 90s) maintains p99 latency within 1.5x baseline and continues to serve reserved capacity while burst consumers are soft-fenced and then throttled.
Billing: Burst consumption is recorded and queryable from API; a simulated tenant consuming 10,000 burst units in a test shows corresponding billing record in billing-staging within 5 minutes.
UI: Console shows burst balance and refill rate for reservations and allows edits with validation; attempting to increase refill rate prompts a confirmation modal that displays cost impact.
Operator: On-call can turn off burst consumption for a tenant via admin API; changes are effective within 30s and logged to audit trails.
Observability: Dashboards correctly reflect soft-fence queue buildup and preemption spikes during load test; alerts fire for preemption rate > 5/min sustained for 3 minutes.
Compatibility: Existing reservations without burst config behave identically to current system (no implicit burst eligibility).
Security: Admin APIs require existing RBAC scope and actions are present in audit logs; security review sign-off is recorded.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: internal dogfooding on staging with 5 internal tenants and operators (2 weeks). Phase 2: opt-in beta for select customers with feature flag (4 weeks). Phase 3: gradual enablement by region and reservation age (6 weeks), followed by global GA. Each phase includes load tests, billing verification, and runbook updates.
rollback_plan: Feature flags at control-plane and per-reservation toggles to disable burst handling and revert to hard-preemption behavior. Metrics and alerts will be used to detect regressions and trigger rollback. Emergency kill switch to immediately deny burst consumption at shard level.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Burst credits enable cost spikes for customers who misconfigure. Mitigation: conservative defaults, confirmation modal in UI, and throttle guardrails.
Risk: Soft-fence queuing increases latency for lower-priority tenants causing poor UX. Mitigation: max queue time, backoff policy, and per-tenant opt-outs.
Risk: Complexity in eviction ordering produces starvation. Mitigation: deterministic ordering policy with fairness windows and telemetry to detect starvation patterns.
operational_playbook: Documented runbook: detection (alerts on preemption rate and reserved p99 violations), immediate actions (disable burst for offending tenant, increase preemption grace period), post-mortem checklist items (billing reconciliation, customer outreach). Include examples of commands and API calls.
notes: This PRD focuses on a pragmatic first iteration that balances predictability for reserved tenants with flexibility for lower-priority workloads. Future iterations may introduce pooled burst markets and cross-tenant borrowing with chargeback.
